deep.reconstruction:
The page is the blank back of a printed Göttingen law-faculty doctoral diploma. The diploma was awarded to Hermann Stockfleth of Hamburg on 29 July 1861, under prorector H. Sauppe and dean G. Francke. The printed text visible on this side is show-through from the recto, in mirror image. Riemann used the back as scrap paper, so the pencil work dates from after mid-1861.

The pencil notes contain no derivation, only sketches and one formula.

(a) Two circles, each with a marked centre point. One has a smaller inner circle labelled 1. This is most naturally a small circle (or the unit circle |z|=1) drawn around a point of the z-plane, i.e. around a branch point.

(b) A cluster of overlapping petal-shaped loops, all passing around or through one central point, with direction arrows. The loops carry labels such as m-1, m, m+1 (possibly m+2), 1 and (m).

(c) A formula, best read as ζ = ∛z (or s = ∛z). The machine reading 'z = ∛z' cannot be right.

(d) A long straight line ending in a small circle. This plausibly represents a cut (Querschnitt or Verzweigungsschnitt) drawn from a branch point, or a path to it.

Interpretation (mine, not certain beyond the general type): Riemann is visualising the function ζ = z^{1/3}. Its Riemann surface over the z-plane has three sheets joined at the branch point z = 0 (and at ∞).
- Write z = r e^{iφ}. The branches are ζ_m = r^{1/3} e^{i(φ + 2πm)/3}, with m taken mod 3.
- One positive circuit around z = 0 sends branch m to branch m+1, i.e. multiplies ζ by e^{2πi/3}. Three circuits return to the start.
- The petal loops labelled m-1, m, m+1 depict this cyclic passage from sheet to sheet around the winding point. Equivalently, they show the images in the ζ-plane of successive circuits: the three sectors of opening 2π/3 around ζ = 0.

No computation is carried out on the page.
errors: No derivation is present, so there is nothing to check for errors. The formula as machine-transcribed ('z = ∛z') is self-contradictory. It is almost certainly a misreading of ζ = ∛z (or s = ∛z).

results.what: Sketch of the three-sheeted branching of ζ = z^{1/3} about z = 0. Loops are labelled by sheet or branch index m-1, m, m+1, indicating cyclic monodromy m → m+1 (mod 3) for each circuit around the branch point.
results.modern_name: Riemann surface of the cube root; monodromy at a branch point (winding point of order 2)

deep.surprise_reason: These are elementary illustrative sketches of a cube-root branch point and its sheet structure. This is exactly the standard material Riemann himself introduced in 1851/1857. The only incidental interest is the dating: the sketches are on the back of an 1861 diploma.

checkable.asserts: Each branch ζ_m = r^{1/3} e^{i(φ+2πm)/3} is a cube root of z = r e^{iφ}; the expression is 0 for integer m.
One circuit around z = 0 (φ → φ+2π) carries branch m to branch m+1; the expression is 0.
Three circuits return to the original branch (monodromy of order 3); the expression is 0.

transcription_corrections: The recipient's name in the show-through is STOCKFLETH (HAMBURGENSI), as on the recto, not 'STOCKHARDT'.
The formula 'z=∛z' should probably read 'ζ = ∛z' (or 's = ∛z'). The first character is a zeta- or s-like glyph, not z.
The loop labels appear to include m-1 (twice), m, m+1 and possibly m+2, plus 1 and (m). They should be read as sheet or branch indices of the cube-root surface.

There is an additional untranscribed sketch: a long straight line ending in a small circle at its left end, possibly a branch cut. There is also a small pencil mark next to the large double circle at left.
